subject: Discovery recap — Observability & evals readiness (dashboards, tracing, golden prompts, rollouts)
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>
To: Claire Huang <c.huang@fincore.io>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.inference>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — Observability & evals readiness (dashboards, tracing, golden prompts, rollouts)

Claire — thanks again for the intro call today. Below is a concise recap of the pain we heard, success criteria you gave, and concrete next steps we agreed on. I left the asks intentionally action-oriented so we can move to a POC checklist quickly.

Pain / triggers
- Seeing unexpected quality regressions after model updates (manual detection takes days).
- Token cost volatility due to bursts and lack of per-route cost visibility.
- No standardized tracing of generation calls -> hard to link latency spikes to specific prompts or cache behavior.

Current stack (what you shared)
- Self-hosted model endpoint cluster (on-prem, Kubernetes) running mixed Open weights.
- Datadog for infra metrics and New Relic APM for app traces.
- Prompt catalog in Confluence; initial golden prompts maintained as a private CSV.

Success criteria (what matters to FinCore)
- Latency: p95 generation < 250ms for priority routes (customer messages).
- Cost: 25–35% effective token-cost reduction through batching/caching within 8 weeks.
- Quality: Regression alerts that catch >90% of semantic regressions for golden prompts; false-positive rate <2%.
- Operational: Rollout guardrail that allows safe canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback on drift/error thresholds.

Observability & Evals asks we discussed
1) Dashboards (Redwood to provide templates):
   - Token-level cost by route and model variant (rolling 1h/24h).
   - Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) per route and region.
   - Golden-prompt pass/fail rate, per-prompt regression trend, and alert summary.
   - KV cache hit ratio and per-request cache latency.
2) Tracing hooks:
   - Span annotations for generation_start, generation_end, model_version, sequence_length, kv_cache_hit (true/false).
   - Trace IDs surfaced in logs to correlate with Datadog/New Relic.
3) Golden prompt set & eval plan:
   - FinCore to share an initial seed set (you indicated ~30 canonical prompts + ~20 paraphrase/variance).
   - Redwood to build an eval harness that runs nightly, computes semantic similarity / hallucination metrics, and raises regression alerts when thresholds are breached.
4) Rollout guardrails and automation:
   - Canary schedule: 5% x 24h -> 25% x 48h -> 100%.
   - Auto-fallback to a safe fallback model if semantic drift > X% or error rate increases by >Y%.

Deliverables and owners (agreed)
- Redwood: eval + observability checklist & example Grafana/Dashboards ("redwood_evals_checklist.xlsx" and dashboard JSON) — target by 2026-05-06 (Markus).
- FinCore: initial golden prompt CSV + contact for infra/tracing owner (Claire / Product Ops) — target by 2026-05-05 (Claire).
- Redwood infra/engineering: sample tracing hook snippet and span naming conventions for your infra team — Connor to produce within 3 business days.

Immediate next steps
- I’ll share the checklist and dashboard templates (Drive link below) by EOD Wednesday (5/6).
- Claire to drop the prompt CSV and confirm a 30–45 minute follow-up with your infra owner to walk tracing integration.

Attachments referenced:
- redwood_evals_checklist.xlsx (checklist + sample dashboards)

If I missed anything, call it out and I’ll update. Thanks again — excited to get this scoped and into a POC.

—
Markus Klein
Enterprise Account Executive

Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Observability & evals readiness (dashboards, tracing, golden prompts, rollouts)

Thanks Markus — this is really helpful and aligned with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications and quick notes: 

- The "canonical" golden prompts we mentioned are customer-facing billing-help and fraud-detection examples — I'll attach an initial CSV (FinCore_golden_prompts_v1.csv) with ~28 rows. Expect another 10–15 paraphrases by Tuesday.
- For rollout fallback: our ops team would prefer defaulting to a smaller quantized model (1.3B) rather than a previous full model. Can Redwood include a quantized fallback plan in the checklist?
- On tracing: we use a truncated trace retention in New Relic (30 days). Would Redwood's suggested spans and correlation IDs fit there? We'll verify with infra owner in the follow-up.

I'll drop the initial prompt CSV now and propose times to sync with our infra owner (Zendesk ticket #4391 included in the attached).  Available slots: Tuesday 5/5 10:00–11:00 PT or Wednesday 5/6 14:00–15:00 PT.

Thanks — Claire
